question: Can actual mechanism sharing be verified on WebArena Docker datasets by extracting accessibility trees from 2-3 shopping stores and measuring mechanism overlap fraction, parameterization prevalence, and duplication fraction — resolving audit VF5 (cross-site mechanism sharing assumed not verified) and unblocking C-LLM-INHERIT experiment design?
hypothesis: WebArena shopping stores (12 instances) share common mechanisms (search, add-to-cart, checkout) with parameterized variations, as suggested by documentation (M1=1.0 cross-site structure). Mechanism overlap fraction across 2-3 stores will be ≥0.5, parameterization prevalence ≥0.3, and duplication fraction <0.8 (tasks are not just copies across stores).
falsifier: ANY of: (1) Mechanism overlap fraction <0.5 across stores — mechanisms are store-specific, not shared. (2) Duplication fraction ≥0.8 — tasks are duplicated across stores, diluting cross-site inheritance meaning. (3) Parameterization prevalence <0.1 — mechanisms lack parameter slots needed for parameterized inheritance. (4) Docker deployment fails or accessibility tree extraction fails on ≥1 store — infrastructure blocks measurement. (5) Documented intent templates do not map to actual interactive elements in accessibility trees — documentation-level structure does not translate to executable mechanisms.
baselines: Corrected Mind2Web M1=0.31 (audit VF1) as comparison for cross-site density
SPIDER 2-site corpus (quotes + books) as lower bound for cross-site diversity
positive_control: Search mechanism (input field + submit button) appears in all sampled stores. Intent templates with variable fields (e.g., product name) are present in task definitions.
null_control: Wikipedia store (if Docker available) does not contain shopping mechanisms (search for product, add-to-cart, checkout).
measurement_validity: Docker Hub am1n3e/webarena-verified-shopping:latest pullable and accessible
Playwright + Chromium functional for accessibility tree extraction
Task definitions parsed from WebArena-Verified dataset (JSON files)
Accessibility tree extraction script validated on at least one store
Frozen random seed for task selection across stores
Raw accessibility trees saved with durable sha256
Intent template mapping verified by manual inspection of 5 tasks
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) mechanism overlap fraction ≥0.5 across stores, AND (2) duplication fraction <0.8, AND (3) parameterization prevalence ≥0.1, AND (4) positive control passes (search mechanism in all stores), AND (5) infrastructure blocks ≤1 store (if 2 stores succeed, proceed), THEN verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. If mechanism overlap fraction <0.5, verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING. If duplication fraction ≥0.8, verdict = MIXED (tasks duplicated, inheritance less meaningful). If infrastructure blocks ≥2 stores, verdict = BLOCKED. If intent templates do not map to accessibility tree elements, verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID (documentation vs execution mismatch).
product_consequence_positive: C-LLM-INHERIT experiment design can proceed with WebArena shopping cross-site pairs. Product lane can design train-on-N-stores, test-on-held-out-stores experiment with verified mechanism sharing. Duplication fraction informs task uniqueness for novelty fraction measurement.
product_consequence_negative: If mechanisms are not shared across stores, C-LLM-INHERIT cannot use WebArena shopping for cross-site inheritance. Product lane must either (a) use a single store with parameter variation, (b) use Mind2Web cross-website splits (if verified), or (c) stay bounded to 2-site corpus. The documentation-level M1=1.0 is shown to be misleading.
estimated_cost: Medium: Docker container deployment for 2-3 stores, Playwright accessibility tree extraction on 20-30 tasks, task definition parsing, mechanism overlap analysis. Estimated 3-4 hours compute. Manual verification of intent template mapping ~1 hour.
expected_information_gain: High: This directly resolves audit VF5 (cross-site mechanism sharing assumed not verified). A clear positive outcome unblocks C-LLM-INHERIT experiment design. A clear negative outcome redirects product lane away from WebArena cross-site inheritance. Even MIXED (duplication high) is valuable because it informs task uniqueness for novelty fraction measurement.
